title: Why do many men tend to idolize horrible male characters in crime/action films?

commenti.body:
The simplest and most obvious answer to your question, which you put in the title, is the subconscious association of yourself with the dominant male on the screen.

But "Fight Club", "Taxi Driver" are different, in my opinion. This is a revolt of a little man against a hypocritical society.

Why do people think this? Nobody in their right mind \*idolizes\* the characters from these films. I've never seen anyone do so. I've never seen anyone provide any examples of doing so. I've only ever seen people claim they are idolized. They simply are films that have iconic lead male characters. it doesn't mean people are idolizing or looking up to them as role models.

You’re not wrong. It’s a phenomenon. Drive guys. Whiplash guys. You played the recorder for 2 weeks in 6th grade but you’re exactly like Whiplash guy? C’mon get real. Take it easy. You don’t see that with The Turning Point, Ice Castles. I’d almost compare it to Star Wars people. The Matrix and cape shit. But women definitely want to be Trinity. Not that The Matrix is bad, the lead actor can’t act but it’s a lovely film. Years ago there were Godafther guys.
